claims.text: Helm is a graduated Cloud Native Computing Foundation project.
Helm is open source under Apache License 2.0 and the Helm project does not ship a commercial tier.

In Helm, resources are installed in a fixed order by Kubernetes kind (defined in helm/helm pkg/release/v1/util/kind_sorter.go); chart authors cannot declare dependencies between resources or subcharts except through hook weights.
In Pulumi, resource ordering derives from the dependency graph: each resource waits for its dependencies to become ready, and independent resources deploy in parallel.
The Helm docs state: "the Kubernetes objects from the charts and all its dependencies are aggregated into a single set; then sorted by type followed by name; and then created/updated in that order."

Helm's install order is a hardcoded list of Kubernetes kinds beginning with PriorityClasses and Namespaces, then Secrets and ConfigMaps, then CustomResourceDefinitions and RBAC, then Services and workloads, with unlisted kinds (including custom resources) last.
Helm uninstall runs the same kind-ordered list in reverse.
Helm sends sorted manifests to the API server in a single pass and does not wait for one resource to become ready before applying the next.
Helm chart dependencies (subcharts) are merged into the parent chart's object set and sorted by kind, so a chart cannot express installing one subchart before another.
Helm chart hooks are ordered with helm.sh/hook-weight annotations, and hook resources are not managed by Helm as part of the release.
Native sequencing for resources and subcharts has been proposed in HIP-0025, which is still a draft.
In Pulumi, passing one resource's output into another or setting the dependsOn resource option creates an edge in the dependency graph.
The Pulumi Kubernetes provider waits for each resource to become ready before creating dependents and deploys independent resources in parallel; deletes follow the graph in reverse.
Pulumi's helm.v4.Chart supports the config.kubernetes.io/depends-on annotation for ordering between objects inside the chart, and dependsOn on the chart for dependencies on outside resources.
Pulumi's dependency-graph ordering with parallel deployment is faster than a strict serial sequence.
Helm records each install or upgrade as a numbered release revision, and helm rollback restores a prior revision.
A failed Pulumi update leaves the stack partially updated, and you roll forward by reverting program code and running pulumi up.
Two patterns cover most production deployments of Pulumi and Helm used together.
Pulumi resolves chart values at deploy time and orders the chart install after its dependencies.
Pulumi creates and deletes resources in dependency order with each resource ready before dependents, unlike Helm's fixed order by kind.
There are three common ways to adopt Pulumi alongside or in place of Helm.
Using Helm charts directly from a Pulumi program is the most common adoption pattern.
Rendering charts with helm template and converting with pulumi convert --from kubernetes produces native Pulumi code.
helm.v4.Chart renders chart templates locally and registers each Kubernetes object as an individual Pulumi resource, so every child shows up in plan output, drift detection, and state.
helm.v3.Release uses the embedded Helm SDK and creates a real Helm release in the cluster, preserving chart hooks, post-rendering, and release history.

Helm merges objects from a chart and its dependencies into a single set, sorts them by Kubernetes kind, and applies them in that order, so declaring a subchart dependency doesn't make it install first.
Pulumi installs a chart after the resources its values depend on.
